========================================================================
PLAYWRIGHT MCP SERVER CONFIGURATION CHEAT SHEET
========================================================================

File Location: .vscode/mcp.json
Used By:       VS Code & GitHub Copilot Agent Session

------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. CORE SCHEMA RULES
------------------------------------------------------------------------
* Do NOT use standard JSON comments (// or /*) inside mcp.json. It will crash.
* Must use "servers" as top-level block in mcp.json (instead of "mcpServers").

------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. BROWSER & EMULATION PROFILES
------------------------------------------------------------------------

[A] DESKTOP PLAYWRIGHT CHROMIUM BINARY (Default Engine)
    "args": ["-y", "@playwright/mcp", "--headless=false", "--browser=chromium"]

[B] DESKTOP GOOGLE CHROME (Uses your local system Chrome installation)
    "args": ["-y", "@playwright/mcp", "--headless=false", "--browser=chrome"]

[C] MOBILE IPHONE EMULATION (Auto-configures viewports and touch inputs)
    "args": ["-y", "@playwright/mcp", "--headless=false", "--device=iPhone 14"]

[D] MOBILE ANDROID EMULATION
    "args": ["-y", "@playwright/mcp", "--headless=false", "--device=Pixel 7"]

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. IMPORTANT LAUNCH RULES
------------------------------------------------------------------------
* Never combine "--browser" and "--device" flags in the same args array. 
If a device is specified, Playwright selects the correct engine automatically.
* To switch profiles, simply copy the lines from the args examples above and paste them over the "args" array in mcp.json.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. MISC NOTES
------------------------------------------------------------------------

[A] --browser options: chromium, chrome, firefox, webkit

[B] --headless options: true (no browser UI) or false (show browser UI)

[C] to verify Playwright MCP server is installed and accessible by Copilot Agent: 
In the agent chat window, submit this prompt: @copilot list available MCP tools
The output from Copilot shows the following tool names under the "Other" category:
openBrowserPage, navigatePage, screenshotPage, clickElement, typeInPage, and runPlaywrightCode

------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. GENERAL INSTALLATION NOTES TO INSTALL PLAYWRIGHT MCP SERVER IN VSCODE AND INTEGRATE WITH COPILOT
------------------------------------------------------------------------
[A] Step 1: Install the Playwright MCP Package 
install the core package inside your existing Playwright project
Run this command in your VS Code terminal in your project root: npm install @playwright/mcp --save-dev

[B] Step 2: Create mcp.json file. This will contain the Playwright MCP Server configuration data.
1. Manually create a folder named .vscode at the root of your project.
2. Create a file named mcp.json inside it.
3. Paste the configuration snippet:
{
  "servers": {
    "playwright": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "@playwright/mcp",
        "--headless=false",
        "--browser=chrome",
      ]
    }
  }
}

[C] Step 3: Grant File Access Permissions
The Playwright MCP server needs permission to look at your existing local code files to interact with them.
Note: this may not be necessary and can be skipped if you are not sure

How to verify your Workspace is Allowed:
Look at the very top of your VS Code window or look for a small "Restricted Mode" status bar banner at the bottom left.
• If you see "Restricted Mode": Click it and select "Trust Workspace". This instantly grants the MCP server the permission it needs to read your Playwright tests.
• If you don't see it: Your project folder is already trusted, meaning you are completely clear to proceed to Step

[D] Step 4: Restart to load changes and run Playwright MCP Server test
1. Reload your VS Code instance (Cmd + Shift + P -> Developer: Reload Window).
2. In the Copilot chat window, make sure you are in Agent mode
3. Submit the following prompt in the chat window: 
"Use your Playwright MCP tools to open a browser window, navigate to https://example.com, take a screenshot, and tell me what the main heading text of the page is."
4. Verify the Copilot agent response is correct for the test result

========================================================================
